timestepPreview.entryHint: See which noise ranges the current settings emphasize and how their losses are weighted.
timestepPreview.title: Training timestep distribution
timestepPreview.shiftIgnored: The current sampling mode does not use discrete_flow_shift; that value is ignored.
timestepPreview.fluxShiftNote: flux_shift uses the preview resolution. During training, each bucket uses its own latent grid position count, so shifts may differ.
timestepPreview.krea2ShiftNote: krea2_shift uses the preview resolution. During training, each bucket uses its own latent grid position count, so shifts may differ.
timestepPreview.densityIgnored: logit_normal/mode changes sampling density only when timestep_sampling=sigma.
timestepPreview.uniformWeightNote: All timesteps use the same loss weight.
timestepPreview.footnote: The curve shows bin-average continuous density; sigma and truncated_logit_normal percentages and medians use the discrete training grid. The loss-weight curve shows the weighting factor. When training at multiple resolutions, preview the main resolutions separately.
timestepPreview.interpretationHint: Percentages show how often each timestep range is sampled. High-noise inputs retain less original image information; low-noise inputs retain more.
timestepPreview.kreaRangeNote: Includes the timestep range. With shape preservation, the curve is truncated to that range. Very narrow ranges may make training fall back to the original distribution and sample outside the range.

lrPreview.internalNote: This optimizer adjusts its learning rate during training; an external scheduler cannot predict its curve.
lrPreview.unsupportedNote: Curve preview is unavailable for this scheduler.
lrPreview.stepCountRequiredNote: This scheduler needs the total training step count. Select a readable dataset and recalculate the training steps.
lrPreview.estimatedStepsNote: Total steps are unknown. This estimate uses {steps} steps and updates when the dataset loads.
lrPreview.endpointJumpNote: At completion, the scheduler jumps to the minimum learning rate. The curve omits this instantaneous jump; the readout at 100% still shows the final value.
lrPreview.invalidNote: Check learning rate, warmup and scheduler parameters. constant requires zero warmup; polynomial requires a base learning rate above 1e-7.
lrPreview.baseGroupNote: Shows the selected component's base learning rate, excluding LoRA+ ratios and per-layer rates.
lrPreview.title: Learning-rate curve preview
lrPreview.chartAlt: Actual learning-rate curve for the current configuration
lrPreview.noStepNote: No total step count is available, so the x-axis shows 0–100% training progress.
lrPreview.estimatedWarmupNote: Total steps are unknown. Warmup is set to {steps}, so this preview uses 10% of training progress until the total is known.
lrPreview.kreaStepCountRequiredNote: This scheduler needs the total training step count. Select a readable dataset and recalculate, or choose steps as the training duration and enter the maximum training steps.
lrPreview.kreaBaseGroupNote: Shows the DiT adapter's scheduled learning rate.

timestepOffset.title: Per-subset sampling offsets
timestepOffset.hint: Negative offsets favor low noise; positive offsets favor high noise. Supported by sigmoid, shift, flux_shift, truncated_logit_normal, and sigma + logit_normal.
timestepOffset.empty: Choose a valid training directory to list numbered subsets such as 10_face.
timestepOffset.rangeWarning: Start within -0.5 to +0.5. Positive values increase high-noise sampling; negative values increase low-noise sampling. Larger absolute values push the distribution toward one end. Check the range percentages after adjusting.

datasetRepeat.title: Dataset repeats
datasetRepeat.hint: Applying this setting renames the folders on disk to update their repeat counts.
datasetRepeat.locked: Locked while a training task is running.
datasetRepeat.selectDir: Select a training dataset directory first.
datasetRepeat.noSubsets: No numbered subset folder here, such as 10_face.
datasetRepeat.invalidRow: Repeats must be a whole number from 1 to 999.

errors.invalidSubsetName: Subset folder must be named like 10_face: {name}
errors.invalidRepeats: Repeats must be a whole number.
errors.duplicateTarget: Two subsets would end up with the same name: {name}
errors.rollbackFailed: Some folders could not be rolled back. Affected subset offsets were cleared. Restore the original names using these paths, then recalculate steps and set the offsets again: {reason}
errors.trainingActive: Cannot rename dataset folders while a training task is running.

shapePreview.w1Help: The first Kronecker factor in LoKr, stored as a full matrix or formed by multiplying two low-rank matrices.
shapePreview.w2Help: The second Kronecker factor in LoKr. Its Kronecker product with W1 forms the weight update matrix.
shapePreview.scaleHelp: The coefficient applied to the weight update matrix, determined by the effective Alpha, Rank, and scaling method.
shapePreview.rankHelp: Controls low-rank factor dimensions. Once a LoKr factor uses full storage, increasing Rank no longer adds parameters to that factor.
shapePreview.alphaHelp: Together with Rank, controls update scaling without changing matrix shapes or file size. This is the effective value for the selected layer.
shapePreview.factorHelp: Controls how LoKr splits input and output dimensions, affecting W1/W2 shapes, parameter counts, and full-storage thresholds.
shapePreview.thresholdHelp: W2 switches to full storage when this layer's Rank reaches this value. Full Matrix forces full storage at any Rank.
shapePreview.sizeHelp: Saved weight size for all layers in this group, determined by matrix shapes, layer count, and save precision. The total file estimate is at the top.
shapePreview.paramHelp: Trainable parameters for one layer; the percentage compares them with the original full weight matrix.
shapePreview.estimateTimeout: The estimate request timed out. Check the remote service or SSH connection, then click Structure preview to retry.
shapePreview.empty: No trainable modules selected by this configuration.
shapePreview.title: Matrix structure preview
shapePreview.scaleForced: 1 (full W1 and W2 force α = rank)
shapePreview.factorAutoNote: factor = -1: split automatically into out = {outL} × {outK}, in = {inM} × {inN}.
shapePreview.w2AutoFullNote: Rank {rank} reaches this layer's W2 full-matrix threshold, max({outK}, {inN}) / 2, so W2 is not low-rank factorized. Other layers are evaluated separately.
shapePreview.w2FullMatrixNote: Full Matrix is on: W2 always stays a full matrix, and raising Rank no longer adds w2 parameters.
shapePreview.w1LowRankNote: decompose_both applies: rank {rank} is below {threshold}, so W1 is low-rank too.
shapePreview.w1StaysFullNote: Decompose both factors is enabled, but Rank {rank} reaches this layer's threshold {threshold}, so W1 stays a full matrix.
shapePreview.unbalancedNote: unbalanced_factorization is on: the two blocks on the output side are swapped.
shapePreview.rsLoraNote: rs_lora is on: scaling uses α / √rank instead of α / rank.
shapePreview.useScalarNote: use_scalar is on: the whole ΔW is multiplied by a learnable scalar.
shapePreview.convNote: conv_dim = {dim} applies to non-1×1 convolutions. This diagram shows a linear layer.
shapePreview.doraNote: DoRA is on: it stores {count} extra magnitude parameters along the {axis} axis.
shapePreview.llmAdapterNote: LLM Adapter layers are trained as well and have different shapes.
shapePreview.adalnNote: AdaLN modulation layers are trained as well and have different shapes.
shapePreview.unknown: Structure preview is not available for this network module.
shapePreview.loraCaption: ΔW = B × A, then multiplied by the scaling factor
shapePreview.lohaCaption: ΔW = (B₁ × A₁) ⊙ (B₂ × A₂), then multiplied by the scaling factor
shapePreview.kronCaption: The weight is split by factor into two Kronecker blocks: out = {outL} × {outK}, in = {inM} × {inN}
shapePreview.kronFormula: ΔW = {w1} ⊗ {w2}, then multiplied by the scaling factor
shapePreview.kronFormulaScale1: ΔW = {w1} ⊗ {w2}, with the scaling factor fixed at 1
shapePreview.diagramAlt: Weight decomposition diagram for the current configuration
shapePreview.footnote: Matrix shapes and parameter counts come from a network built with the current settings. File size includes weights and their index, excluding training metadata and optimizer state. Shapes use a logarithmic scale; dimensions are labeled.

opt.convrot_int8_bwd_bf16: Default; dequantizes weights for more accurate gradients.
opt.convrot_int8_bwd_int8: INT8 gradient computation introduces quantization error and requires CUDA and Triton. Usually offers no noticeable speedup with gradient checkpointing.
opt.model_train_type_sdxl-lora: Stable Diffusion XL series LoRA training
opt.save_model_as_pt: Saves LoRA weights using PyTorch serialization with the .pt extension.
opt.save_model_as_ckpt: PyTorch LoRA weights with a .ckpt extension
opt.save_precision_fp16: 2 bytes per weight value, with a smaller numerical range than BF16.
opt.save_precision_bf16: 2 bytes per weight value, with a wider numerical range than FP16. Both use the same weight-data size.
opt.save_precision_float: 4 bytes per weight value. Weight data is twice the size of FP16 or BF16.
opt.lr_scheduler_cosine_with_restarts: Lowers the learning rate along a cosine curve. Restarts when the cycle count is greater than 1.
opt.lr_scheduler_cosine: Cosine annealing, smoothly reduces learning rate
opt.lr_scheduler_constant: Keeps the scheduled learning rate constant.
opt.lr_scheduler_inverse_sqrt: After warmup, lowers the learning rate in proportion to the inverse square root of the step count.
opt.lr_scheduler_cosine_with_min_lr: After warmup, lowers the learning rate along a cosine curve with a configurable minimum rate ratio.
opt.lr_scheduler_warmup_stable_decay: Warms up, holds the learning rate constant, then decays over the specified final steps.
opt.lr_scheduler_piecewise_constant: Applies a constant learning-rate multiplier in each interval, using cumulative step boundaries.
opt.wsd_warmup_linear: Rises at a constant rate to the base learning rate.
opt.wsd_warmup_cosine: Cosine rise: slow at the ends, faster in the middle.
opt.wsd_warmup_1-sqrt: Rises slowly at first, then accelerates.
opt.wsd_decay_linear: Falls at a constant rate to the minimum learning rate.
opt.wsd_decay_cosine: Follows a cosine curve; with cycles set to 1, falls slowly at the ends and faster in the middle.
opt.wsd_decay_1-sqrt: Falls quickly at first, then slows down.
opt.optimizer_type_AdamW: Uses moving averages of gradients and squared gradients to scale updates, with separate weight decay.
opt.optimizer_type_AdamW8bit: Reduces memory use by storing larger optimizer states in 8-bit format.
opt.optimizer_type_PagedAdamW8bit: AdamW8bit with paging: swaps optimizer states to system RAM under memory pressure, slowing training while swapping.
opt.optimizer_type_StableAdamW: Adds RMS clipping of update magnitude on top of AdamW, capping per-step update size.
opt.optimizer_type_Lion: Updates parameters using the signs of combined gradients and historical momentum. Use Lion's starting learning rate after switching.
opt.optimizer_type_Lion8bit: Stores Lion momentum for larger tensors in 8-bit, while smaller tensors keep 32-bit state.
opt.optimizer_type_PagedLion8bit: Lion8bit with paging: swaps momentum states to system RAM under memory pressure.
opt.optimizer_type_Prodigy: Automatically estimates the step-size scale D during training. This trainer fixes the learning-rate multiplier at 1.0. Inspect D in the logs.
opt.optimizer_type_ProdigyPlus: Prodigy combined with Schedule-Free: automatic step-size estimation plus in-optimizer scheduling.
opt.optimizer_type_Automagic3: Adjusts per-group learning rates from gradient-sign history with internal update clipping.
opt.optimizer_type_AdaFactor: Uses row and column statistics for factorable tensors to reduce second-moment storage. With relative_step enabled, computes step size from the training step count.
opt.optimizer_type_AdamWScheduleFree: Maintains training and averaged weights, using averaged weights for evaluation and saving. Uses internal warmup and disables external learning-rate scheduling.
opt.optimizer_type_CAME: Uses factorized second moments, residual-confidence scaling, and internal RMS clipping to reduce state storage for factorable tensors.
opt.optimizer_type_EmoSens: Adjusts the learning rate based on loss changes and suggests when to stop. Does not stop training automatically.
opt.optimizer_type_Muon: Accumulates gradient momentum, then approximately orthogonalizes the update of 2-D matrices.
opt.optimizer_type_LoRAMuon: Processes both LoRA factors jointly to reduce sensitivity to how their scales are distributed. Supports native Anima LoRA, native Krea 2 LoRA and Krea 2 LoCon. Tune the learning rate separately.
opt.krea_lycoris_algo_locon: Uses LyCORIS low-rank matrices for weight updates. Krea 2 targets are all Linear layers; network_dim sets their rank.
opt.optimizer_type_Adan: Tracks gradients, changes between consecutive gradients, and squared lookahead statistics using three beta coefficients.
opt.optimizer_type_AdEMAMix: Maintains short- and long-term gradient averages. Beta1 and Beta3 set history retention; Alpha sets the long-term momentum contribution.
opt.optimizer_type_AdEMAMix8bit: AdEMAMix with 8-bit optimizer states; same update formula.
opt.optimizer_type_LoRARite: Designed for paired LoRA factors to reduce sensitivity to equivalent representations.
opt.optimizer_type_SOAP: Uses gradient correlations to choose an update basis, then applies Adam-style updates. Adds computation compared with ordinary AdamW.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_uniform: Samples timesteps uniformly across the full noise range.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_sigmoid: Maps normal random values through sigmoid, producing a distribution concentrated toward the middle of the timestep range.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_sigma: Uses weighting_scheme to select uniform, Logit-Normal, or Mode timestep density.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_shift: Samples with sigmoid first, then shifts the distribution by fixed discrete_flow_shift.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_krea2_shift: Computes the Krea 2 shift from the current resolution instead of using fixed discrete_flow_shift.
opt.krea_timestep_sampling_logsnr: Samples from the Log-SNR normal distribution defined by logit_mean and logit_std.
opt.krea_weighting_scheme_none: Changes neither timestep density nor per-timestep Loss weights.
opt.krea_lr_scheduler_inverse_sqrt: After linear warmup, decays in inverse proportion to the square root of the training step.
opt.krea_lr_scheduler_cosine_with_min_lr: Cosine decay down to the configured minimum learning rate.
opt.krea_lr_scheduler_warmup_stable_decay: Runs warmup, a stable constant phase, then a final decay phase.
opt.krea_lr_scheduler_rex: Warms from the minimum learning rate to the base value, then follows the REX curve back to the minimum.
opt.krea_attention_sdpa: Native PyTorch attention; no extra installation
opt.krea_network_module_lora: Native Krea 2 LoRA; represents weight updates with low-rank matrices.
opt.krea_network_module_lycoris: Train LoCon, LoHa or LoKr with LyCORIS; choose the algorithm below. Krea2 targets Linear layers, where LoCon uses low-rank matrices.
opt.krea_training_duration_epochs: Train for dataset passes, including configured repeats. Total update steps depend on batch size, gradient accumulation and other settings.
opt.krea_training_duration_steps: Train for optimizer updates. Accumulated batches count as one step; training can end partway through an epoch.
opt.krea_attention_flash_attn: FlashAttention; install in Environment, with installation checked before training
opt.loss_type_l1: Mean absolute error. Doubling an error doubles its loss contribution.
opt.loss_type_l2: Mean squared error. Doubling an error quadruples its loss contribution.
opt.loss_type_huber: This project uses a smooth Huber formula: approximately quadratic for small errors and linear for large errors, with the threshold setting the transition range.
opt.loss_type_smooth_l1: Uses the same smooth curve as this project's Huber, without multiplying by the threshold coefficient. The difference is loss scaling.
opt.network_module_networks_lora: Standard LoRA network for SD/SDXL architectures
opt.network_module_networks_loha: Represents weight changes as an elementwise product of two low-rank products, giving a different parameterization from standard LoRA.
opt.network_module_networks_lokr: Represents weight changes with a Kronecker product of two smaller matrices. Decomposition settings control the parameter count.
opt.network_module_lycoris_kohya: LyCORIS Library, supporting LoCon, LoHa, LoKr, and related modes
opt.lycoris_algo_locon: Represents weight changes with low-rank matrices and supports a separate rank for convolution layers.
opt.lycoris_algo_loha: Represents weight changes with the elementwise product of two low-rank matrix products.
opt.lycoris_algo_lokr: Represents weight changes with a Kronecker product of two matrices. Rank and decomposition settings decide whether the factors are further low-rank factorized.
opt.lycoris_preset_full: Matches preset target modules in the backbone and text encoder, with convolution adapters enabled. Train normalization layers controls norms separately.
opt.lycoris_preset_full_lin: Matches preset target modules in the backbone and text encoder, without convolution adapters.
opt.lycoris_preset_attn_mlp: Matches preset backbone targets including Transformer, embedding, and output modules, plus text-encoder targets. No convolution adapters. For Anima, Align with sd-scripts default excludes modulation, embedding, and output layers.
opt.lycoris_preset_attn_only: Matches attention class names listed in the preset. Does not match the current Anima backbone.
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_only: Matches preset backbone targets with convolution adapters enabled. Does not target the text encoder.
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_transformer: Matches preset backbone targets including Transformer, embedding, and output modules. No text-encoder targets or convolution adapters.
opt.lycoris_preset_unet_convblock: UNet convolution and ResNet blocks only; not applicable to DiT
opt.lycoris_kernel_backend_triton: Uses Triton; requires a compatible environment.
opt.lycoris_kernel_backend_tilelang: Fused TileLang kernels; falls back automatically when not installed
opt.lycoris_kernel_backend_compile: Compiles each op; the first run is slower
opt.sample_sampler_ddim: DDIM updates. The current SDXL preview path adds no extra random noise at each step.
opt.sample_sampler_euler: First-order Euler updates of the latents.
opt.sample_sampler_euler_a: Euler updates with random noise added during denoising.
opt.sample_sampler_heun: Second-order predictor-corrector updates, with two model evaluations in intermediate denoising intervals.
opt.sample_sampler_dpmsolver_plus: Multistep DPM updates based on denoised predictions, reusing predictions from earlier steps.
opt.mixed_precision_bf16: BFloat16 mixed precision; requires BF16 GPU support
opt.mixed_precision_no: Disables mixed-precision computation. Component-specific fixed precision and quantization settings still apply.
opt.timestep_sampling_sigma: Samples from a discrete noise schedule; the distribution depends on the weighting scheme and timestep shift
opt.timestep_sampling_uniform: Samples uniformly across the full timestep range
opt.timestep_sampling_sigmoid: Favors medium noise by default; the distribution width is adjustable
opt.timestep_sampling_shift: Applies a fixed shift to the sigmoid distribution to favor higher or lower noise
opt.weighting_scheme_sigma_sqrt: Weights loss by 1 / sigma²; does not change the sampling distribution
opt.weighting_scheme_logit_normal: Samples timesteps from a Logit-Normal distribution only with sigma sampling; adds no loss weighting
opt.weighting_scheme_mode: Samples timesteps from the Mode distribution only with sigma sampling; adds no loss weighting
opt.weighting_scheme_cosmap: Gives medium noise more loss weight than the two ends, without changing sampling frequency.
opt.weighting_scheme_uniform: Uses the same loss weight at every timestep. Does not change how often each timestep is sampled.
opt.attn_mode_torch: Built-in PyTorch SDPA; automatically selects an available kernel. No extra installation needed.
opt.huber_schedule_snr: Sets the threshold from the current noise level: near 1 at low noise and near huber_c at high noise. Does not use huber_scale.
opt.huber_schedule_constant: Uses huber_c × huber_scale at every noise timestep.
opt.huber_schedule_exponential: As the noise timestep increases, the threshold changes exponentially from 1 toward huber_c, then is multiplied by huber_scale. Does not decay with training progress.
opt.dynamo_backend_inductor: Default compilation backend focused on performance
opt.dynamo_backend_eager: Immediate execution backend focused on compatibility and debugging
opt.dynamo_backend_cudagraphs: Uses CUDA Graph to reduce kernel launch overhead
opt.timestep_sampling_flux_shift: Automatically adjusts the shift based on the training image's latent grid size
opt.timestep_sampling_truncated_logit_normal: Truncates and rescales a logit-normal distribution, with optional uniform sampling
opt.compile_backend_inductor: Default backend focused on runtime performance
opt.compile_backend_eager: Immediate execution backend focused on compatibility
opt.compile_backend_cudagraphs: Reduces kernel launch overhead via CUDA Graph
opt.compile_mode_reduce_overhead: Uses CUDA Graphs to reduce Python and kernel-launch overhead, caching extra workspace. Requires a supported CUDA graph.
opt.compile_mode_max_autotune: Benchmarks operator implementations during compilation and selects the faster ones, with supported CUDA Graph optimizations enabled.
opt.compile_mode_max_autotune_no_cudagraphs: Benchmarks operator implementations during compilation without enabling CUDA Graphs.
opt.compile_dynamic_auto: Compiles for the current dimensions first, then attempts dynamic shapes when dimensions change.
opt.compile_dynamic_true: Compiles for dynamic input dimensions so one graph can support multiple bucket sizes.
opt.compile_dynamic_false: Compiles for fixed input dimensions and creates new compiled variants when dimensions change.
opt.sample_sampler_lms: Linear multistep updates using earlier predictions. Requires SciPy.
opt.sample_sampler_dpmsingle: Single-step DPM method, with multiple predictions within each solver step.
opt.sample_sampler_dpm_2: Second-order DPM updates using a prediction at an intermediate position.
opt.sample_sampler_dpm_2_a: Second-order DPM updates with random noise added during denoising.
opt.sample_sampler_pndm: Combines Runge-Kutta and linear multistep updates of the latents.
opt.foreach_trueDesc: Batch updates for usually faster execution, potentially using more peak VRAM.
opt.foreach_falseDesc: Update tensors individually; try this if VRAM is tight.
